proposal.reason: Trial 1 on the primary split used word-only logistic regression with C=0.3 and achieved macro_f1 0.498404 with class recalls [1.0, 0.030303], showing the spam class was almost never recovered. The next primary-search candidate should test a representation that adds character n-grams and uses less regularization, because character features can capture spam patterns that word-only features may miss while retaining word-level signal.
proposal.review: The selected candidate is an available registered single_text logistic candidate with one expected classifier fit, within the remaining fit allowance. This is a primary-search choice only; no formal test is available, and the prior trial is evidence rather than proof that this change will improve macro_f1.
proposal.hypothesis: Combining word and character n-gram features with C=3.0 may improve spam recall relative to the word-only C=0.3 baseline by representing obfuscated or character-level spam cues and reducing underfitting of the minority class.
proposal.uncertainty: The direction and magnitude of macro_f1 change are unknown. The prior trial shows severe spam recall failure, but it does not establish that word_char features or C=3.0 will fix it; they may overfit or still miss spam. No formal test is available to the agent.
